<p class="cycle-role">Choices about which uncertainties and evidence gaps merit investigation.</p>

<p class="page-deck"><strong>Which new evidence would most improve urban climate decisions?</strong></p>

We develop approaches for identifying where new cases, evaluations, datasets and forms of knowledge could resolve consequential uncertainty or expand the learning options available to cities.

::: {.notice}
**Part of a connected learning cycle.** Projects and cities may enter at different points. Evidence about consequences can revise judgements about existing knowledge and where new evidence matters.
:::

## Questions the lab investigates

- Which unresolved questions could materially alter an urban climate decision?
- Where could a new case, evaluation or dataset clarify an important mechanism?
- Which systematic exclusions limit the learning options available to multiple cities?

## Analytical boundary

- Treating every geographical evidence gap as equally important.
- Tool or dataset announcements without a consequential evidence question.
- Automated research-priority scores or context-free rankings of evidence needs.
